translationRepairs: On a later birthday celebration the emperor had Ji play polo against the chief ministers, and Ji won.
On a later birthday celebration the emperor had Ji play the board game shuo (握槊) against the chief ministers, and Ji won.
握槊 is a tables/board game (related to shuanglu), not polo; the idiomatic English mistranslates the game.
Later he attended the Tian Shou festival; the emperor ordered Ji and the great ministers to play polo; Ji won.
Later he attended the Tian Shou festival; the emperor ordered Ji and the great ministers to play the board game shuo (握槊); Ji won.
握槊 is a board game, not polo; literal English should not say polo.
The emperor said, "This repays your blunt honesty at the polo game."
The emperor said, "This repays your blunt honesty at the shuo (board-game) match."
Follows the 握槊 mistranslation in s0042; correct to board-game/shuo.
The emperor said: "This rewards your forthright counsel in the polo match."
The emperor said: "This rewards your forthright counsel in the shuo (board-game) match."
Follows the 握槊 mistranslation; literal should not say polo.
Yanlun was clever by nature and skilled at winning Empress Dowager Dao's favor, and through this he rose to considerable trust and preferment.
Yanlun was clever by nature and skilled at winning Daohe's favor, and through this he rose to considerable trust and preferment.
Chinese has 悼合 as a personal name; idiomatic English inserts 'Empress Dowager' not present in the Chinese.
